connectorUiConfig.title: QCrypton PQC Proxy (via Codeless Connector Framework)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The [QCrypton PQC Proxy](https://www.qcrypton.com/) data connector ingests TLS handshake telemetry from PQC Proxy instances into Microsoft Sentinel through the QCrypton API. PQC Proxy is a hybrid post-quantum TLS 1.3 reverse proxy (X25519MLKEM768) that terminates TLS in front of any HTTP backend. This connector streams handshake negotiation results, PQC downgrade events, certificate health signals, and connection metrics into the **PQCProxy_CL** table.

sampleQueries.description: PQC handshake adoption rate in the last 24h
sampleQueries.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventType == 'handshake'
| summarize PQC = countif(QuantumPosture == 'pqc-hybrid'), Classical = countif(QuantumPosture == 'classical'), Downgraded = countif(QuantumPosture == 'downgraded') by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| render timechart

sampleQueries.description: All PQC downgrade events in the last 24h
sampleQueries.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventType == 'downgrade'
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ClientIP, NegotiatedGroup, OfferedGroups, CipherSuite
| order by TimeGenerated desc

sampleQueries.description: Certificate expiry status across all proxies
sampleQueries.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where EventType == 'cert_expiry'
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId
| project ProxyHost, CertPath, CertExpiryDays
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

dataTypes.name: PQCProxy_CL
dataTypes.lastDataReceivedQuery:
PQCProxy_CL
| summarize Time = max(TimeGenerated)
| where isnotempty(Time)

instructionSteps.title: Connect QCrypton PQC Proxy to Microsoft Sentinel

parameters.content: This connector polls the QCrypton API to retrieve TLS handshake telemetry from PQC Proxy instances and ingest them into the **PQCProxy_CL** table in your Log Analytics workspace.

#### 1. Deploy PQC Proxy
Deploy QCrypton PQC Proxy as a sidecar container in front of your HTTP backends. Follow the [deployment guide](https://www.qcrypton.com/docs/pqc-proxy) for Docker, Azure VM, or DigitalOcean.

#### 2. API Key
Obtain your QCrypton API key from the [QCrypton Portal](https://portal.qcrypton.com). Navigate to **Settings > API Keys** and generate a key with read access to proxy telemetry.

#### 3. API Server URL
Enter the base URL of your QCrypton API server. The default is `https://api.qcrypton.com`. If you use a dedicated or regional instance, enter the URL provided by QCrypton.

parameters.label: QCrypton API Server URL
parameters.name: apiServerUrl
parameters.description: Enter the QCrypton API base URL. Do not include a trailing slash or path.

dataFlows.transformKql: source | extend TimeGenerated = iff(isnull(TimeGenerated), now(), TimeGenerated) | project TimeGenerated, ProxyInstanceId, ProxyHost, EventType, ClientIP, NegotiatedGroup, OfferedGroups, CipherSuite, HttpStatus, RequestLatencyMs, UpstreamTarget, QuantumPosture, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, ErrorMessage, Metadata

schema.name: PQCProxy_CL
schema.description: TLS handshake telemetry from QCrypton PQC Proxy instances. Contains per-request hybrid post-quantum key exchange negotiation results, PQC downgrade events, certificate health, and connection metrics.

columns.name: ProxyInstanceId
columns.description: Unique identifier for the PQC Proxy instance.

columns.name: ProxyHost
columns.description: Hostname or IP where the PQC Proxy is running.

columns.name: EventType
columns.description: Type of event: handshake, downgrade, cert_expiry, tls_error, upstream_error.

columns.name: ClientIP
columns.description: Remote IP address of the connecting client.

columns.name: NegotiatedGroup
columns.description: TLS key exchange group negotiated (e.g., X25519MLKEM768, X25519, P-256).

columns.name: OfferedGroups
columns.description: Colon-separated list of key exchange groups offered by the client.

columns.name: HttpStatus
columns.description: HTTP response status code. 0 for non-HTTP events.

columns.name: UpstreamTarget
columns.description: Backend upstream URL the request was proxied to.

columns.name: QuantumPosture
columns.description: PQC posture of the handshake: pqc-hybrid, classical, or downgraded.

columns.name: CertPath
columns.description: Path to the TLS certificate served by the proxy.

columns.name: CertExpiryDays
columns.description: Days until the served certificate expires. Null for non-cert events.

columns.name: ErrorMessage
columns.description: Error details for tls_error and upstream_error events.

properties.description: PQCDowngradeDetected_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A TLS handshake completed where the client offered a post-quantum hybrid key exchange group
(X25519MLKEM768 or X25519Kyber768Draft00) but the negotiation fell back to a classical group
(X25519 or P-256). This may indicate a misconfigured PQC Proxy, a middlebox stripping PQC
groups from ClientHello, or an active downgrade attack. Investigate the proxy configuration
and network path between client and proxy.
properties.displayName: PQC downgrade detected - client offered hybrid but classical was negotiated
properties.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "downgrade"
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, ClientIP, NegotiatedGroup, OfferedGroups, CipherSuite, Metadata
| order by TimeGenerated desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCProxy Analytics Rule 1

properties.displayName: PQC downgrade detected - client offered hybrid but classical was negotiated

properties.description: ProxyCertExpiringSoon_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A PQC Proxy instance is serving a TLS certificate that expires within the next 30 days.
Certificate renewal should be performed before expiry to avoid service disruption. If the
certificate is renewed, ensure the replacement uses a PQ-hybrid or classical algorithm
compatible with TLS 1.3 and the configured key exchange groups.
properties.displayName: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 30 days
properties.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "cert_expiry"
| where CertExpiryDays <= 30
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId, CertPath
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, Metadata
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCProxy Analytics Rule 2

properties.displayName: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 30 days

properties.description: ProxyCertCriticalExpiry_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A PQC Proxy instance is serving a TLS certificate that expires within the next 7 days.
Immediate certificate renewal is required to prevent service outage. Clients will receive
TLS errors once the certificate expires, breaking all PQC-protected connections through
this proxy.
properties.displayName: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 7 days - immediate renewal required
properties.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "cert_expiry"
| where CertExpiryDays <= 7
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by ProxyInstanceId, CertPath
| project TimeGenerated, ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, CertPath, CertExpiryDays, Metadata
| order by CertExpiryDays asc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCProxy Analytics Rule 3

properties.displayName: PQC Proxy certificate expiring within 7 days - immediate renewal required

properties.description: TLSHandshakeFailureSpike_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

An elevated rate of TLS handshake failures was detected on a PQC Proxy instance within the
last hour. This may indicate clients using incompatible TLS libraries, expired or invalid
certificates, a denial-of-service attempt, or network-level interference with the TLS
handshake. Investigate the error messages and client IPs to determine the root cause.
properties.displayName: TLS handshake failure spike on PQC Proxy
properties.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "tls_error"
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), DistinctClients = dcount(ClientIP), Errors = make_set(ErrorMessage, 5) by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId
| where ErrorCount > 10
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, ErrorCount, DistinctClients, Errors
| order by ErrorCount desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCProxy Analytics Rule 4

properties.displayName: TLS handshake failure spike on PQC Proxy

properties.description: UpstreamConnectionFailures_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A PQC Proxy instance is experiencing elevated upstream connection failures when forwarding
requests to its backend service. This may indicate the backend is down, overloaded, or
unreachable. While the PQC Proxy TLS termination is functioning correctly, clients will
receive 502/504 errors until the backend recovers.
properties.displayName: Upstream backend connection failures on PQC Proxy
properties.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "upstream_error"
| summarize ErrorCount = count(), Errors = make_set(ErrorMessage, 5) by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, UpstreamTarget
| where ErrorCount > 5
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, UpstreamTarget, ErrorCount, Errors
| order by ErrorCount desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCProxy Analytics Rule 5

properties.displayName: Upstream backend connection failures on PQC Proxy

properties.description: HighLegacyClientRate_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

More than 50% of TLS handshakes on a PQC Proxy instance in the last 24 hours used classical
(non-PQC) key exchange because clients did not offer any post-quantum groups. This is an
adoption tracking signal - these clients are not protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later
attacks. Consider requiring client TLS library upgrades or communicating PQC requirements
to connecting services.
properties.displayName: High percentage of clients connecting without PQC support
properties.query:
PQCProxy_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| summarize Total = count(), Classical = countif(QuantumPosture == "classical") by ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId
| extend ClassicalPct = round(100.0 * Classical / Total, 1)
| where ClassicalPct > 50
| project ProxyHost, ProxyInstanceId, Total, Classical, ClassicalPct
| order by ClassicalPct desc

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

QCrypton PQC Proxy is a hybrid post-quantum TLS 1.3 reverse proxy (X25519MLKEM768) that protects traffic against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. This Microsoft Sentinel solution ingests handshake telemetry from PQC Proxy instances, enabling detection of PQC downgrade attacks, certificate health monitoring, and post-quantum adoption tracking across your infrastructure. Ships with 1 data connector, 6 analytic rules, workbook, and Teams-notification playbook.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in Preview state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs:

• Microsoft Sentinel Codeless Connector Framework

Data Connectors: 1, Workbooks: 1, Analytic Rules: 6, Playbooks: 1
